title: Request-context-aware circuit breaker with graded fallback scripts
creator: Asha Menon
description: Implement a request-context-aware circuit breaker that evaluates trip thresholds using request importance signals (tenant priority, request freshness, SLA class), latency quantiles, and replica health. When the breaker trips, orchestrate graded fallback scripts: 1) local prefix/KV cache response (if matched), 2) lower-fidelity model variant with deterministic cost/latency profile, 3) queued background execution with an immediate degraded placeholder, and 4) tenant-notified degraded-mode indicator. Ensure multi-region failover semantics and SLO alignment so trips only occur when doing so improves end-to-end SLO attainment and protects global tail latency.
acceptance_criteria: Breaker can be configured at per-dependency, per-model, and per-tenant scope via runtime config
Trip decision uses configurable composite score: weighted(latency_p95, error_rate, replica_health, tenant_priority, recent_slo_miss_rate)
Fallback scripts are chainable and annotated in the tracing headers for observability
End-to-end tests show reduced global p99 tail latency under simulated regional overload without increasing total SLO misses by >5%
Canary rollout across regions + automatic rollback on increased error-rate (observability hooks present)
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Breaker decision engine - implement composite score computation and rule DSL (server-side)
Phase 2: Runtime integration - expose per-entity config, integrate with routing and KV cache
Phase 3: Fallback script framework - implement ordered handlers (cache, model-variant, degraded-placeholder, notify)
Phase 4: Multi-region semantics - ensure consistent trip reasoning and safe cross-region failover with sticky fallbacks
Phase 5: Observability & rollout - dashboards, traces, canary, and rollback logic
testing_plan: Unit tests for composite score computation and DSL parsing
Integration tests simulating: regional overload, replica flapping, noisy-tenant storm
Chaos tests that kill model replicas and validate fallback ordering and no double-billing
Load tests measuring p95/p99 improvement and impact on total successful responses
SR (security review) checklist: ensure fallback doesn't leak sensitive content from cached responses
rollout_strategy: Start with internal prod cluster subset (low-impact tenants) for 48h
Canary to single non-critical region with traffic shaping (5%->25%->100% over 72h)
Automated rollback triggers: increased request error-rate > 2x baseline OR unexplained SLO regressions
Full rollout tied to runtime-1.22 release and accompanied by docs and runbook
risks_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect weighting causes false trips -> mitigation: default conservative weights and offline tuning job
Risk: Fallback increases model drift or degraded output -> mitigation: mark fallbacks in responses and add quality-monitoring label
Risk: Cross-region inconsistencies -> mitigation: use deterministic evaluation for trip decisions and ship region-scope overrides
Risk: Cache fallback serving stale private data -> mitigation: enforce tenant-scoped cache keys and TTL validation
qa_checks: Tracing includes breaker decision payload and fallback step ID
Audit log entries for every trip/fallback event with tenant and request_id
Load shed metrics surfaced per-tenant and per-model in Console
Regression alerts for quality-monitoring tied to prompt-set evals
notes: Early spike analysis (dashboards/replay) suggests large tenants with long-context summarization workloads are primary trip candidates
Trade-off: favor conservative trips to avoid customer-visible failures; allow billing-transparent degraded placeholders for non-critical requests
